text_visible: Modern AI often defines agency as reward maximization: specify an objective, then learn to optimize it through interaction.

This paper argues for an alternative foundation in which purposeful behavior emerges from learning computable generators in complete action-observation histories, with a crucial epistemic rule: actions are interventions, not evidence; so beliefs update only through the world's responses to what the agent does.

text_visible: Reinforcement learning has become the default language for "purposeful" behavior in machine learning: an agent is modeled as maximizing expected cumulative reward [15, 41].
A competing intuition is both older and more general: much of intelligent behavior is acquired second-hand.
In the broadest sense, imitation is the uptake of a pattern—a regularity in behavior, language, or demonstration—and its conversion into a first-person capacity to act.
